## Sprint B2 — Async Fixes (ClickHouse Service Layer)
**Goal:** The service-layer functions in `clickhouse.py` also call `client.query()` synchronously inside `async def`. These weren't fixed in the prior session.

**Pattern to use everywhere:**
```python
import asyncio
result = await asyncio.to_thread(client.query, sql, parameters=params)
```

### US-B201 — Fix `apps/api/app/services/clickhouse.py`
> As the event loop, I need all ClickHouse calls to be non-blocking.

| | |
|---|---|
| **File** | `apps/api/app/services/clickhouse.py` |
| **What to do** | Find every `client.query(...)` call inside an `async def`. Wrap each one: `result = await asyncio.to_thread(client.query, sql, parameters=params)`. Add `import asyncio` at the top if not present. |
| **Edge case** | `get_clickhouse_client()` factory function stays sync — that's fine. Only wrap the actual query calls. |
| **DONE when** | No bare `client.query(...)` calls remain in any `async def` function in the file |

### US-B303 — Automated KOL Wallet Seeding (Amendment — added Mar 2026)
> As the system, I automatically populate the known_wallets table from public leaderboard data so the table stays current without manual effort.

|---|---|

| **Source 1** | KOLscan leaderboard (`kolscan.io/leaderboard`) — scrapes top ~50 traders via cheerio. Extracts wallet address from `href="/account/{addr}"` and name from `<h1 style="font-size:20px">` inside the account link. |

## Sprint B4 — Signal Detection Engine
**Goal:** The signals feed currently only reads from the `signals` table — nothing writes to it. This is the biggest missing piece. Signals must be auto-detected from incoming webhook transactions.

### US-B401 — Signal Detection on Webhook Ingest
> As a user on the Signals page, I see real signals being generated from on-chain activity, not an empty feed.

| | |
|---|---|
| **File** | `apps/api/app/routers/webhooks.py` |
| **What** | After ingesting a transaction and evaluating alerts, run signal detection. If any signal condition matches, write a row to the `signals` ClickHouse table. |
| **Signal types to detect** | See table below |
| **DONE when** | A test webhook with a large transfer produces a row in `signals` table within 5 seconds |

**Signal Detection Rules:**

| Signal Type | Condition | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| `large_transfer` | SOL transfer > 1000 SOL OR token transfer > $50,000 USD value | PROBABLE |
| `new_wallet_funded` | Receiving wallet has 0 prior transactions, funded ≥ 0.1 SOL | SUSPECTED |
| `known_wallet_active` | Sender or receiver matches a `known_wallets` entry with `status=approved` | CONFIRMED |
| `multiple_sends` | Same sender → 5+ different recipients in same block | SUSPECTED |
| `exchange_withdrawal` | Known exchange wallet → fresh wallet (0 prior txs) | PROBABLE |

**Signal schema (ClickHouse `signals` table):**
```sql
INSERT INTO signals (
  id, signal_type, confidence, wallet_address,
  related_address, token_mint, amount_sol, amount_usd,
  tx_signature, metadata, detected_at
) VALUES (...)
```

### US-B402 — Signal Confidence Scoring
> As an analyst, I trust signals that come with calibrated confidence levels.

| | |
|---|---|
| **File** | `apps/api/app/routers/webhooks.py` signal detection function |
| **What** | Each signal written to ClickHouse must include a `confidence` value: `CONFIRMED`, `PROBABLE`, or `SUSPECTED` |
| **Rules** | See confidence column in table above |
| **DONE when** | All signals in the feed have a non-null confidence field |

## Sprint B7 — Rate Limiting by User Tier
**Goal:** Currently all users (free and pro) get the same rate limits. The code has `# TODO: pull from user tier.` comments.

### US-B701 — Tier-Aware Rate Limiting
> As a Pro user, I get higher API rate limits than free tier users.

| | |
|---|---|
| **File** | `apps/api/app/middleware/rate_limit.py` (or wherever rate limiting is implemented) |
| **Free limits** | 60 requests/minute, 10 AI queries/day |
| **Pro limits** | 300 requests/minute, 100 AI queries/day |
| **Enterprise** | Unlimited (skip rate limiting middleware) |
| **How** | On each request, if auth token present, call `supabase_svc.get_user_tier(user_id)`. Use tier to select limit. Cache tier in Redis (5-minute TTL) to avoid DB hit per request. |
| **DONE when** | A free user hitting AI endpoint 11 times in a day gets HTTP 429. Pro user does not. |
